# I1
Verdict: accept-w-rev
CRITICAL: 0
MAJOR: 1; [evidence-incomplete] The central output-related consistency claim lacks a verified statistical variable, objective-to-code correspondence and attributable performance evidence in the supplied packet (prior_work.md, C1–C3).
Headline: An implemented output-related phase constraint supports a bounded investigation, but its independent contribution remains unverified (prior_work.md, C1–C3).
Occupation: N1 establishes Laplace residual priors and unfolded updates, N2 establishes learned multimodal phase processing and input/output spectral association, and N5–N7 establish spectral saliency reconstruction; the remaining difference is the specific RGB-depth-saliency consistency constraint. Coverage is adequate for this component-level assessment, but establishes neither a complete occupying result nor zero target-setting hits; N3 and N4 have limited method coverage (prior_work.md, N1–N7, Papers Read).
Experiment: The proposed NJU2K/NLPR training and STERE/LFSD testing, three seeds, matched-capacity fusion, phase-only, no-penalty and Gaussian/Laplace arms provide useful attribution controls. The proposed success thresholds are +0.01 S-measure and 5% relative MAE improvement on both held-out sets without worse corruption sensitivity; matched-control equivalence or absent intervention effects kills the hypothesis. The strongest contemporary RGB-D baseline and exact phase intervention still require specification (candidate.json, Minimal Falsification Experiment).
Estimand: The planned comparisons target the incremental segmentation benefit of learned phase updates and the Laplace constraint under matched resources, which aligns with the residual novelty claim; distributional fit alone cannot establish that benefit. Mechanistic interpretation also requires defining the residual and intervention signal explicitly (candidate.json, Minimal Falsification Experiment; prior_work.md, C2–C3).
Payoff: A useful new payoff would be independently attributable accuracy or robustness improvement from the output-related constraint over matched fusion and frequency controls. The nine-dataset superiority statement supplies no effect sizes or attribution, so it cannot establish a clear-accept increment (prior_work.md, C1–C3, N1–N2).
Feasibility: The proposed two-researcher, two-A100, one-week initial probe is plausibly bounded through fixed datasets and reused pretraining; its multi-arm, three-seed workload lacks runtime estimates, so completion within one week is unverified. The proposed nine-dataset expansion is conditional on successful attribution (candidate.json, Minimal Falsification Experiment).
History: unavailable.
Reason: Accept with revisions because the specific constraint remains potentially distinct, implementation evidence supports an exploration path, and the proposed probe can test its value (prior_work.md, C1–C2, N1–N7; candidate.json, Minimal Falsification Experiment). [evidence-incomplete] Unverified statistical correspondence and incremental gains prevent Strong Accept; the transfer exception also lacks demonstrated zero target-setting hits, a setting-forced adaptation and realized clear-accept signal (prior_work.md, C1–C3, Strongest Counterexample; review_contract.md, Review Calibration). These gaps do not establish a defective method or omitted author experiments.
